<!-- This is an auto-generated comment by CodeRabbit -->

`agencyTimezone()` reimplements `time.LoadLocation` here instead of reusing the existing `loadAgencyLocation(agencyID, timezone)` helper in `timezone_helper.go`, which every other handler that resolves an agency's timezone already calls (`stops_for_location_handler.go`, `trips_for_route_handler.go`, `schedule_for_route_handler.go`, `vehicles_for_agency_handler.go`, etc.).

More importantly, those call sites log a `Warn` with the agency ID and error when the load fails (see `stops_for_location_handler.go:268-273`), giving operators visibility into a misconfigured `agency.txt` timezone. Here the error is silently swallowed and falls back to UTC with no log output, so the same misconfiguration is invisible specifically on `current-time.json`.

Worth reusing `loadAgencyLocation` and logging on the fallback path for consistency with the rest of the codebase (see CONTRIBUTING.md's Code Reuse section).

`agencyTimezone()` has three fallback branches — `GetAgencies` error, empty agency list, and an invalid timezone string — but only the happy path (valid `America/Los_Angeles`) is covered here. Per CONTRIBUTING.md, "every new branch or condition introduced by a PR needs test coverage." Worth adding cases for the fallback branches (e.g. via a mocked/empty agency list) so a future change to the fallback behavior doesn't ship silently broken.
